name: Grade 6 T1: Web Design and Copyright
description: Website features, web page layout, navigation, image choice, copyright, credit, and fair use.

words.definition: A collection of related web pages that people can visit online.
words.example: The class reviewed a website before planning their own page.

words.definition: One page inside a website.
words.example: The student created one web page about recycling.

words.definition: The language used to structure many web pages.
words.example: HTML can tell a browser which text is a heading.

words.definition: The name or main heading of a page or section.
words.example: A clear title helps visitors know the topic.

words.definition: A top area or heading section on a web page.
words.example: The header included the page title and a short introduction.

words.definition: A part of a page that groups related information.
words.example: The first section explained the purpose of the project.

words.definition: The arrangement of text, images, and other parts on a page.
words.example: The layout made the web page easy to read.

words.definition: The way users move around a website.
words.example: Clear navigation helps visitors find pages quickly.

words.definition: A list of links that helps people move through a website.
words.example: The menu linked to the home page and project page.

words.definition: Clickable text, an image, or a button that opens another page or place.
words.example: The student tested the link to make sure it worked.

words.definition: The main or first page of a website.
words.example: The home page introduced the website topic.

words.definition: The people a web page is made for.
words.example: The audience for the page was sixth graders.

words.definition: Digital content such as text, images, audio, or video.
words.example: The page used media to explain the topic clearly.

words.definition: A picture or visual used in a digital project.
words.example: The image supported the web page message.

words.definition: A legal protection that gives creators control over how their work is used.
words.example: Copyright means we cannot use every picture we find online.

words.definition: A note that names the creator or source of something used in a project.
words.example: The credit line showed where the image came from.

words.definition: The place where information, an image, or media came from.
words.example: The student recorded the source of the photo.

words.definition: A limited way to use copyrighted work for purposes such as learning, commentary, or teaching.
words.example: Fair use still requires careful choices and credit.

words.definition: Allowed to use without normal copyright restrictions, often with clear rules.
words.example: The student chose a copyright-free image for the website.

words.definition: Rules that explain how a person may use someone else's work.
words.example: The image license said the creator needed credit.

words.definition: A way to see how a page or project will look before publishing or sharing it.
words.example: The student used preview to check the page on a smaller screen.

words.definition: To judge how well something works using clear criteria.
words.example: The class evaluated the web page with a checklist.

words.definition: A list used to check that important parts are complete.
words.example: The website checklist reminded students to test links.

words.definition: How easy and comfortable something is to use.
words.example: Good usability helps visitors find information quickly.
